messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: fleet-monitor detected ECC/Xid error rate spike (3xx -> 2k/hr) across us-central-rack7..9; ~12 GPUs flapping, capacity down ~6% (auto-retry failures trending). Logs + links: https://dash.redwood/alerts/2190004321
sarah.eng: seeing the same on the per-model SLO dashboard — p50 latency for short completions +25ms, error rate +0.8% at peak. Noticed increases since 05:10 UTC.
jordan.sre: grabbing logs from the agent: looks like repeated 'Xid 43' and thermal sensor oscillations in the same hosts. pushing node list in a sec.
lee.infra: pasted node list: rack7-node[03..08], rack8-node02, rack9-node01,04. NVML shows temps toggling between 72C and 86C every 3-4 minutes for the impacted cards.
alec: any recent driver/firmware pushes? we did a small kernel roll last night to 6.1.14 but only on canaries — not these racks.
sarah.eng: driver/firmware history: rack7/8/9 got firmware bundle 2.3.1 on 2190004000 during a maintenance window (ops-run). That was mainly bmc/psu patches.
infra-bot: DEPLOY: firmware-bundle-2.3.1 applied to rack7-9 @2190004000 — change ticket #CH-4523.
jordan.sre: sample nvlog snippet from rack7-node05:
```
[2026-09-03T05:22:11Z] Xid 43: Gpu context killed
[2026-09-03T05:22:12Z] ecc_count increase: card0 += 12
[2026-09-03T05:22:15Z] temp: gpu0 85C -> 72C -> 84C (oscillation)
[2026-09-03T05:22:20Z] nvlink reset invoked
```
lee.infra: looks like thermal hysteresis on the fan controller after the firmware bump. fans spin up/down too slowly, causing short-term overheating and ECC blips.
alec: ok — mitigation options:
- drain affected nodes (evacuate jobs) and mark for hardware-validation
- rollback firmware to 2.3.0 on those racks (requires coord with field ops)
- enable aggressive fan curve as emergency workaround if available
- route traffic to dedicated pool / increase burst capacity (cost)
oncall-sre: priority: protect SLOs. Recommend immediate soft-drain of the 8 most-impacted nodes, keep 4 in warm-spare for hotfix testing.
sarah.eng: agree with soft-drain. start with rack7-node03..08 and rack9-node01
jordan.sre: running drain script now: `./ops/drain-nodes --nodes rack7-node03,rack7-node04,rack7-node05,rack7-node06,rack7-node07,rack7-node08,rack9-node01 --soft --evict=best-effort`
lee.infra: starting aggressive fan profile on rack8 via IPMI override: `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0x66 0x01 0x00` — that's experimental, will monitor temps.
(just a note: IPMI commands vary by vendor, doing this as a stopgap)
alec: good. also please open a HW ticket with vendor (ACME-GPU) for replacement if ECC counts keep rising. set severity = S2.
jordan.sre: drain progress: 6/8 nodes drained, 2 still live — some pods failed eviction due to local checkpoint locks, rescheduling with force eviction now.
sarah.eng: rerouting short completion traffic to dedicated-pool-a to reduce tail latency. updating routing rules in infra-router (10s rollout).
infra-bot: ROUTER: route change applied to infra-router at 2190005100 — redirecting ~12% of short-completion traffic to dedicated-pool-a.
alec: cost note: dedicated-pool-a autoscale will likely spin up extra capacity — estimated extra spend $2.8k/day if this runs for 48 hrs.
sarah.eng: that's acceptable vs SLO breach. please keep finance informed if we exceed 48h.
oncall-sre: monitoring: error-rate down from +0.8% to +0.15% after drains + routing. p50 latency mostly recovered, p95 still elevated on a few models.
jordan.sre: nvml counters on the drained nodes still show ECC increments — pushing nodal logs to /logs/hw/2190004321/ for vendor.
lee.infra: scheduled field ops to swap suspect cards in rack7 on 2190004322 (UTC). vendor engineer assigned: @ACME-Field (ticket CH-4523).
alec: plan for next 24h:
- keep nodes drained + in hardware queue
- attempt fan-profile rollback if safe
- if ECC persists after card swap, rollback firmware bundle 2.3.1 on the rack
- keep routing to dedicated-pool with cost cap $6k

Please ack so we can close the incident channel and track in CH-4523.
sarah.eng: ack. thanks team — solid quick response. adding short postmortem checklist to the ticket.
jordan.sre: one more note: add nn-monitor rule to detect thermal oscillation pattern (freq + amplitude) so we catch this earlier.
infra-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation in place, severity lowered to S3 at 2190007200. Auto-reminder in 12h for status update.
oncall-sre: closing slack triage thread, will update CH-4523 with timeline and artifacts. If anyone sees re-escalation, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
